question: Should OpenClaw ship enabled-by-default agent-authored dashboard widgets behind this approval, unauthenticated serving, sandbox, and prompt-bridge model after the concrete defects are fixed?
rationale: This introduces browser execution of agent-authored code, an unauthenticated asset route, persistent approval state, and prompt dispatch; implementation correctness alone cannot approve that product and security boundary.

options.title: Ship after hardening
options.body: Fix all blockers, prove the complete lifecycle on the exact head, and land only with explicit product and security approval.

options.title: Land trusted workspaces first
options.body: Split out SQLite workspaces and built-in widgets while deferring custom-widget execution and its unauthenticated route.

options.title: Do not ship custom widgets
options.body: Redesign or close the custom-widget portion if maintainers do not want agent-authored browser code in the bundled dashboard.

recommendation.title: Ship after hardening
recommendation.body: Fix all blockers, prove the complete lifecycle on the exact head, and land only with explicit product and security approval.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the current-main bundled-view seam and authored the branch integration and security hardening, making him the best history-backed decision router.
